clue.text: Attack little devil firing gun

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil

indicators.note: a gun firing goes off, so its letters are set off into a new order

explanation.surface: A small devil opens fire with a gun in an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firing' rearranges GUN into UGN, which follows IMP.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn a claim is to challenge or assail it as false.

clue.text: Popular spell repressing conservative inclination

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: repressing means holding something down within, so the spell word encloses the conservative letter

parts.note: a stint is a spell of work

explanation.surface: A popular charm holds back a natural Tory leaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repressing' puts C inside STINT, giving STINCT after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An instinct is an innate tendency or natural leaning.

clue.text: Drama by writer which gives childish amusement

parts.note: a play is a piece of drama
a pen is a writing instrument, a crossword 'writer'

explanation.surface: A play by an author that only entertains children.
explanation.definitionFit: A playpen is an enclosure where a toddler is put to play safely.

clue.text: Ecologist's estimate, we hear, of fruit

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: an environmentalist, a Green, makes a gauge or estimate: a green gauge

explanation.surface: An environmentalist's guess about some fruit, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a green-skinned variety of plum.

clue.text: Drolly go off American flag

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, signalling the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A wry instruction to leave, beside the Stars and Stripes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the letters of DROLLY GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Glory is the nickname of the US Stars and Stripes.

clue.text: Liberal type of Pole at 90?

definitions.meaning: tolerant and broad-minded, especially in religious matters
someone living at latitude 90 degrees, where the North or South Pole lies

explanation.surface: A broad-minded Polish person who is ninety years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' and '90' suggest a Polish nonagenarian; the poles of the Earth sit at latitude 90 degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: A latitudinarian allows wide latitude in belief, being tolerant of differing views.

clue.text: Reptile could give good sound echo

indicators.note: sound tells us to take how the next word is pronounced, not how it is spelt

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like ECKO

explanation.surface: A lizard might make a fine echoing noise.
explanation.walkthrough: ECHO is pronounced ECKO, which follows G.
explanation.definitionFit: A gecko is a small climbing lizard of warm countries.

clue.text: Green mineral and oil applied to grape plant

indicators.note: applied suggests the oil is worked over, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: grapes grow on a vine

explanation.surface: Oil is rubbed on a grapevine, along with some green rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applied' rearranges OIL into OLI, which goes before VINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivine is an olive-green silicate rock mineral, the gem form being peridot.

clue.text: Eye Pip letting out cry of delight

indicators.note: letting out suggests the letters are loosened and released into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The character Pip from Dickens lets out a joyful shout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letting out' rearranges the letters of EYE PIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Yippee is an exclamation of glee or excitement.

clue.text: Healthy men one's seen rowing here?

definitions.text: Healthy men one's seen rowing here?

indicators.note: rowing suggests oars churning, so the letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored and the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A question of where fit men are spotted pulling oars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rowing' rearranges HEALTHY MEN ONES; the whole clue also describes the regatta town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxfordshire town hosts the famous annual Royal Regatta for oarsmen.

clue.text: Step taken by socialist — in this direction?

parts.note: a stage is a step in a process
the political left includes socialists

explanation.surface: A move made by a left-winger, pointing towards the way to go.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: stage left is a theatre direction, so a step taken that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage left is the side of a stage to an actor's left as they face the audience.

clue.text: Sound of bird tucking right into fried potato

indicators.note: tucking something in places it within another thing
into completes the instruction that the right letter goes inside the fried potato

parts.note: a chip is a fried potato strip

explanation.surface: A bird tucks right into a chip and makes a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking ... into' puts R inside CHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A chirp is the short high call a small bird makes.

clue.text: Drive to conceal a name to form jury

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something inside, so the drive word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: to impel is to drive forward

explanation.surface: An urge to hide a name when choosing a jury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to conceal' puts A and N inside IMPEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To impanel is to enrol people on a panel, especially a list of jurors.

clue.text: Cheat identified by one of the tables? Almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: schoolchildren learn the times tables, one being the two times table

explanation.surface: Someone cheats at a card table and is almost caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of the tables' means a multiplication table, not furniture; 'Almost' cuts the last letter of TWO TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: To two-time a partner is to be unfaithful by secretly seeing someone else.

clue.text: Is unable, when in Scotland, to find Hebridean island

definitions.meaning: a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone in Scotland cannot reach a Hebridean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Canna is both the Scots form of 'cannot' and a small Inner Hebridean isle.

clue.text: One shouting about party backed Alpine singer

indicators.note: about means going round, so the shouter's word surrounds the party

parts.note: a yeller is a person who yells

indicators.note: backed means the party word is read in reverse

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A shouter at a party backed a singer from the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns DO into OD, and 'about' puts YELLER round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yodelling is the warbling song style of Swiss and Tyrolean mountain folk.

clue.text: Form of closure with a person ultimately thought of as liberating?

indicators.note: form of means a reshaped version, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A kind of shutdown with someone regarded as freeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' rearranges CLOSURE plus A plus N, the last letter of 'person'; 'liberating' is slang for stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Larcenous means thieving, and to liberate goods is a jocular phrase for pinching them.

clue.text: Back support leads to further apprehension

parts.note: the rear is the back
a rest is a support, as an armrest

explanation.surface: A back brace prompts more worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apprehension' looks like anxiety, but it means capture by police.
explanation.definitionFit: A re-arrest is a second taking into custody.

clue.text: Man's no angler, as it turns out

indicators.note: turns out signals the letters are turned into a different order

explanation.surface: It emerges a certain man is not a fisherman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it turns out' rearranges NO ANGLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Algernon is a male first name.

clue.text: Want to get established as most tedious?

parts.note: to long for something is to want it

explanation.surface: Wanting to become settled is the dullest ambition.
explanation.definitionFit: The longest talk or book drags on the most, and so is the most boring.

clue.text: Author, one you'd find in library mostly

indicators.note: mostly means all but the end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a reader is someone found in a library

explanation.surface: A writer is someone found in a library, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of READER.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade was the Victorian novelist of The Cloister and the Hearth.

clue.text: A movement associated with eastern fertility goddess

parts.note: a start is a sudden jump or movement

explanation.surface: A movement linked with a goddess of fertility in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Astarte was the Phoenician deity of love and fecundity.

clue.text: Military commander has timeless weapon

indicators.note: timeless means without time, and T is the abbreviation for time, so it is removed

parts.note: a shotgun is a weapon

explanation.surface: A commander has a weapon that never ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' takes T out of SHOTGUN.
explanation.definitionFit: The shogun was the hereditary general who ruled Japan for centuries.

clue.text: Nun is embarrassed in very hard description of Attila

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the pencil marking

parts.note: HH is the pencil-grade marking for very hard

indicators.note: embarrassed means discomposed, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A nun is flustered by a very harsh account of Attila.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embarrassed' rearranges NUN IS, and 'in' puts that inside HH.
explanation.definitionFit: Attila was king of the Huns, so he is fittingly described by the adjective for that people.

clue.text: One old group of detectives rejected description of compound

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the detectives' letters are reversed

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: An old squad of detectives was turned down while describing a mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns CID into DIC; the CID is the plain-clothes branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: Iodic describes a chemical containing iodine, as in iodic acid.

clue.text: Come down to earth to go in for exam again

definitions.meaning: of a spacecraft, return through the atmosphere
enter a second time for a test

explanation.surface: A student comes back to reality and resits the exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsule re-enters the atmosphere, and a candidate re-enters for a test.

clue.text: A vice like this would be admitted

definitions.text: A vice like this would be admitted

parts.words: A vice like this would be admitted
parts.note: put the letter A before the vice meant and the result is a word meaning admitted or conceded

explanation.surface: A failing of this kind would be confessed.
explanation.walkthrough: A followed by the vice spells AGREED, meaning admitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed is one of the seven deadly sins, an excessive desire for wealth or food.

clue.text: Plant surprisingly made money in Belgium when about to engage women

indicators.note: surprisingly means unexpectedly, so the letters are rearranged
to engage is to take in, so the reversed money holds the women letter
about means turned round, so the currency is read backwards

parts.note: the euro is Belgium's currency

explanation.surface: Someone surprisingly earned money in Belgium while trying to hire women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges MADE into MEAD; 'about' turns EURO into ORUE, and 'to engage' puts W inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Meadow rue is a herbaceous perennial with feathery leaves, genus Thalictrum.

clue.text: Mark on patient's wallet

parts.note: a note is a mark or sign
a doctor refers to a patient as a case

explanation.surface: Someone notices the wallet belongs to a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A notecase is an old word for a wallet for holding banknotes.

clue.text: Maintain Romeo will be taken in by something of value

indicators.note: taken in by means placed inside, so the Romeo letter goes inside the valuable

parts.note: an asset is something of value
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo will be fooled by a treasure, it is claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be taken in by' puts R inside ASSET.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert a view is to declare it firmly, to hold it as true.
